The area below the curve from x=-1 to x=1 is ∫_{-1}^{1} 4/(1+x^2) dx = 4[arctan x]_{-1}^{1} = 4(π/4 - (-π/4)) = 2π. Therefore the shaded area = rectangle area - area below the curve = 8 - 2π.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a rectangle with vertical sides at x = -1 and x = 1, bottom on the x-axis, and top at y = 4, with the curve y = 4/(1+x^2) passing through the top point (0,4). The shaded region is the part of this rectangle lying above the curve. Compute rectangle area as width 2 times height 4, giving 8. Then subtract the area under the curve from x = -1 to x = 1: ∫_{-1}^{1} 4/(1+x^2) dx = 4[arctan x]_{-1}^{1} = 2π. The shaded area is 8 - 2π.

method.method_draft: Read from the diagram that the shaded region is symmetric about the y-axis because the rectangle is centered from x = -1 to x = 1 and the curve has its peak at (0,4). Compute only the right half of the shaded area, from x = 0 to x = 1, using vertical slices: slice height is 4 - 4/(1+x^2).
